Non-Disclosure Agreement
This Non-Disclosure Agreement is hereby incorporated into the existing Employment Agreement between {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} or its subsidiaries (hereinafter referred as the Company) and the undersigned employee.

As an employee, contractor or temporary staff of {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}, the employee may have access to confidential information including customer information, financial or business information obtained through their association with {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}.

Confidential information is considered invaluable and sensitive and unauthorized disclosure of the same can cause significant monetary and reputational damages to {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}. Legal systems have strict provisions in ensuring protection of confidential information in any form. Inappropriate disclosure of confidential information by an employee may result in the imposition of monetary penalties and/or initiation of legal proceedings.

In consideration of the above, the employee hereby acknowledges and agrees that the:

1. Employee will not access confidential information for which they have no legitimate need to know and for which they are not the authorized user. This includes accessing their own confidential information without proper access permission.

2. Employee will not in any way divulge, copy, release, sell, loan, review, alter or destroy any confidential information unless expressly permitted by existing policy except as properly approved in writing by an authorized officer of {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} within the scope of my association with {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}.

3. Employee will not utilize another user's password in order to access any system nor will he/she reveal his/her computer credentials to anyone else for any reason. The Employee accepts responsibility and understands that he/she will be held accountable for all activities occurring under his/her computer credentials.

4. If the employee observes or has knowledge of unauthorized access or divulgence of confidential information, he/she will report it immediately to the reporting manager and/or Human Resource Manager and/or Managing Director.

5. The employee agrees not to seek personal benefit or permit others to benefit personally by any confidential information that he/she may have access to or that he/she accesses as an unauthorized user.

6. The employee understands that all information, regardless of the media on which it is stored (paper, computer, mobile, videos, recorders, etc.), the system which processes it (computers, voice mail, mobile, faxes, etc.), or the methods by which it is moved (electronic mail, face to face conversation, etc.) is the property of {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} and shall not be used inappropriately or for personal gain.

7. The employee also understands that {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} reserves the right to inspect or monitor any company owned, leased, or controlled computer, computer device, network, computer facility, storage device, voice mail or telephone system at any time for any reason and that {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} may divulge any information found during such inspections or monitoring to any party it deems appropriate. The employee understands that he/she should not consider electronic communications to be either private or secure, nor have an expectation of privacy in anything he/she creates, stores, sends, or receives on the computer and network.
8. The employee agrees to abide by all {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} rules and regulations as specified in company policies unless specifically altered by a separate contractual agreement.

9. The employee understands that his/her failure to comply with this Agreement may result in corrective action which might include, but is not limited to, termination of employment and/or loss of privileges within {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }} as well as potential civil or criminal penalties.

All training materials and handouts given to the trainees are exclusive property of {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}. No part of these documents can be duplicated or reproduced without the prior written permission of {{ company_doc.company_name or doc.company }}.

The term of employment shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue unless terminated in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.

The Employee shall be subject to a probation period based on the applicable employee level, as specified in the Probation Period Schedule below. During the Probation Period, the Employee shall not be entitled to any Performance-Linked Incentive under this Agreement.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Fixed Compensation: In consideration of the Employee's services, the Company shall pay the Employee an annual fixed compensation of INR {{ ctc_display }}, inclusive of all statutory contributions and subject to applicable tax deductions, payable in monthly instalments in accordance with the Company's payroll cycle.

Performance-Linked Incentive: In addition to the Fixed Compensation, the Employee may be eligible for a performance-linked incentive (the "Performance Incentive"), subject to the following:

Quantum: as determined by the Company, based on such performance metrics as may be notified by the Company from time to time;

Performance Period: each financial year (1 April to 31 March), or such other period as may be determined by the Company;

Conditions: the Performance Incentive shall be subject to the following conditions:

the Employee must be in active, confirmed employment with the Company on the date of disbursement, and must not have tendered resignation or been served a notice of termination;

the Employee must not be in breach of any material obligation under this Agreement;

the Performance Incentive shall be subject to applicable tax deductions and statutory contributions;

the Company reserves the right to claw back all or part of the Performance Incentive in the event of any material misrepresentation, fraud or wilful breach by the Employee, for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the date of each disbursement; and

Employee Fraternization Policy at {{ company_name }}

1. Introduction
At {{ company_name }}, we are committed to fostering a professional and inclusive work environment. This Employee Fraternization Policy is designed to establish clear guidelines regarding personal relationships within the workplace to prevent conflicts of interest, maintain a fair and transparent work environment, and uphold professional standards.
2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, including full-time, part-time, temporary, and contract workers, as well as interns and volunteers.
3. Definition of Personal Relationships
Personal relationships covered by this policy include, but are not limited to, romantic relationships, dating, familial relationships (including spouses and siblings).
4. Disclosure Requirements
Employees are required to disclose personal relationships if one individual holds a position of authority over the other. However, voluntary disclosure is encouraged to address potential conflicts proactively.
5. Conflict of Interest
a. Reporting Relationships: Employees in a reporting or supervisory relationship with a family member (spouse or sibling) must disclose the relationship to HR. In such cases, arrangements may be made to mitigate any conflicts of interest, such as reassignment of responsibilities or supervision.
b. Professional Decision-Making: Employees involved in a personal relationship should ensure that their personal ties do not compromise their professional judgment, decisions, or actions.
6. Conduct Expectations
All employees are expected to maintain a professional and respectful workplace environment. Personal relationships, including those with spouses and siblings, should not interfere with work responsibilities or create a disruptive atmosphere.
7. Impact on the Workplace
Employees with personal relationships, including spouses and siblings, should be mindful of how their interactions may be perceived by colleagues. Any behavior that disrupts the workplace or creates discomfort for others is not acceptable.
8. Consensual Relationships
While consensual relationships between adults are a personal matter, employees are expected to be aware of the potential impact of their relationships on the workplace.
9. Reporting Violations
Any Employee who become aware of any violations of this policy should report them to HR or another designated authority. Reports will be handled confidentially and investigated promptly.
10. Retaliation Protection
An Employee who make good faith reports under this policy will not face retaliation. Retaliation against any employee for reporting a violation of this policy is strictly prohibited.
11. Penalties for Non-Compliance
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary actions, ranging from counselling and reassignment of duties to suspension or termination of employment, depending on the severity and recurrence of the violation.
12. Review and Updates
This policy will be periodically reviewed to ensure its effectiveness and relevance. Any updates will be communicated to all employees.
